newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil up, expecting cash push.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil up, expecting cash push.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged up slightly late afternoon on Thursday as players geared up in expectation of more agressive buying from local traders despite weaker crude values, brokers said.
"People are expecting more aggressive buying on the physical market and they are bidding the swaps market up," one broker said.
Brokers said May gas oil swaps were quoted at $25.70/25.90 up from Wednesday's $25.60/25.70. They said May traded earlier in the day at $25.65.
Front month balance April traded earlier in the day at $27.05 per barrel, and was last quoted at $27.00/$27.20.
Physical gas oil buying eased this week after record purchases last week of 1.35 million barrels on Tuesday and 1.91 million barrels on Friday for a total of 3.25 million.
So far this week, the traders bought a mere 450,000-barrel for a grand total of over 14 million barrels purchased since March 3.
Brent June contract settled lower in London on Wednesday at $17.81, breaking the previous support of $17.90 and opened on Thursday to last trade down nine cents at $17.72.
Fuel oil swaps were steady again in expectation of physical purchases with May traded earlier in the day at $98.25 per tonne, brokers said.
May was last quoted at $98.80/98.75 for May largely unchanged from Wednesday despite the crude fall.
